title: Threshold tiling
objective: Explain how subtypes with different force thresholds together encode stimulus intensity.

steps.title: A team that covers the range
steps.body: No single afferent type covers the whole range of distension equally well. Instead, different [[DRG]] subtypes have different force **[[threshold|thresholds]]** — some fire to gentle filling, others only to strong, potentially harmful distension. Together they **tile** the intensity range, so the brain can tell 'full' from 'dangerously over-full'.

flag.note: Many low-threshold colon afferents also keep encoding into the noxious range; dedicated high-threshold units add to the top end rather than owning it alone.

steps.prompt: Why have multiple subtypes with different force thresholds instead of one?
options: To encode a range of intensities, from gentle filling to harmful over-distension
To provide spares, so one subtype can stand in for another
Because each threshold matches a different modality, like heat vs stretch
So low-threshold units carry pain and high-threshold units carry fullness
steps.explanation: A set of differently-tuned subtypes spans the intensity range (rate/population coding), letting the system distinguish normal filling from injury-level stretch. A single threshold would compress that range; tiling extends it.

variants.setup: Colon afferents come in low-, mid-, and high-threshold subtypes.
options: Encoding a range of distension intensities
Spare neurons that can stand in for each other
Detecting only the painful stimuli, nothing else
variants.reveal: Tiling thresholds lets the population encode intensity from gentle to harmful.

steps.setup: You selectively silence only the high-threshold colon afferents.
options: Blunted response to strong/noxious distension, with normal responses to gentle filling
Loss of all colon sensation at once, both the gentle filling and the strong distension alike
Paradoxically stronger pain even from gentle, normal filling of the colon
Loss of the response to gentle filling, while strong distension is still detected normally
steps.reveal: High-threshold afferents carry the strong/noxious end of the range, so silencing them should spare gentle-filling sensation but blunt responses to harmful distension — a subtype-specific, testable prediction, and exactly the kind of experiment the lab runs.

variants.prompt: Silencing only high-threshold colon afferents should…
options: Blunt responses to strong distension, spare gentle filling
Remove all colon sensation, gentle and strong alike
Remove gentle-filling sensation, spare strong distension
variants.explanation: High-threshold units carry the noxious end; gentle-filling sensation uses lower-threshold units.

sources.note: DRG subtypes tile the distal colon by force threshold; endings in defined wall layers.

reviewNotes: Threshold tiling / population coding of intensity; subtype silencing.
